notes.text: Scan 075 bears the author's upper-left number 33 and the pale lower-left foliation 74 in another unnamed hand. The foliation is kept separate from his own number. This is a handwritten text sheet with four displayed groups and one oblique marginal note.

The manuscript introduces tubular neighbourhoods T_{(0)}, T_1 and T_d and writes successive expressions for X^{(1)}, X^{(2)} and X^{(d)}. Its final display writes expressions for \Sigma_i. The oblique note records T_d=\bigcup_{i\in I,\delta(i)\leq d}T_i and describes T_i as a vois. tub. de X_i dans X. These statements are attributed to the manuscript; no proof, implication, or equality has been checked in this reading.

The opening brace ends after the second row; the third equality and its de sorte que continuation stand below it. The prose occurrence after dans is the small x^{(1)} supported by p06. The last display writes X_{(d)} with a lowered parenthesized d. These positions and cases are retained without changes prompted by the argument. The isolated upright preceding \Sigma_i is also retained without an assigned operation.

Witness C contains an English editorial sentence inside the last formula, beginning '(48) removes the interiors'. The entire p10 region contains the mathematical handwriting, its cancellations and blank intervening space, but no such sentence. That addition is excluded and logged as absent from the source. Its mathematical assertion was neither used to choose a reading nor checked.

The first T_\alpha in the last display has a predominantly filled raised oval with a tiny internal glint. The dot-leading reading and ring alternative are both preserved. The seven other ringed T occurrences on the page show open centres. The first final union bound has a short almost straight underline beneath \alpha; the second has a wavy stroke beneath j. The manuscript's written decorations are kept separately, without an inferred interpretation.

The live (48) crop shows two tiny isolated points below its equality, near original x676–682 and y1880–1890. Their function and provenance are not established. They are recorded as source-position observations in the audit comment and are not supplied as punctuation or a new formula sign. The clear final point after that display is transcribed.

The first spelling has a large closed terminal loop, supporting standard with standart as an alternative. The later two occurrences have short angular terminal uprights and are transcribed standart. This decision is local to the strokes at each occurrence. The replacement prend is raised above cancelled pose; only de, rather than a duplicate spelling, is crossed after the second occurrence.

The least secure material consists of the two cancelled display numbers, the first cancelled low group, the raised reworked marks, the last cancelled brace/relation, and the head of the final live number's terminal digit. All remain doubtful at their exact positions. Both witnesses' supplied numbers were compared with their contours rather than recovered by sequence. The two marked choices M0645 and M0646 are resolved from their whole-expression crops.
